topic_name: A Story of Numbers: Reema's Curiosity
title: These strange marks are numbers
description: Shows that the strange wedge marks on an old loose page are numbers written about 4000 years ago.

title: Number names grow by tens
description: Shows that old Indian number names went up in powers of 10, each one 10 times the one before.

title: One stick for every cow
description: Shows one-to-one mapping: each returning cow is paired with one stick, and the 2 sticks left over are the 2 missing cows.

title: Letters as a counting sequence
description: Shows counting with the letters a to z: the 20th object gets t, and a 27th object has no letter left.

title: A number system is a fixed sequence
description: Shows that counting maps each object to the next symbol of a standard sequence in a fixed order, and that the written symbols are numerals.

title: Add two stick piles by joining
description: Shows the simplest stick arithmetic without number names: adding two collections by putting them together.

title: 29 notches read as fives
description: Shows the 29 notches of the old tally bone grouped into 5 groups of five and 4 more.

title: Five is ukasar ukasar urapon
description: Shows how the Gumulgal name for 5 is built from twos and one: 2 + 2 + 1.

title: 1345 in fives needs 269 symbols
description: Shows that writing 1345 with only a symbol for five needs 269 copies of that symbol, far too many.

title: Two urapons make an ukasar
description: Shows adding Gumulgal numbers by joining their words, with two urapons regrouped into one ukasar.

title: 2367 grouped into landmarks
description: Shows 2367 written as MMCCCLXVII, with each group of symbols bracketed by the landmark value it adds.

title: Regroup the Roman symbols
description: Shows adding CCXXXII and CCCCXIII by counting each symbol and regrouping into bigger landmarks.

title: Regroup to add LXXXVII and LXXVIII
description: Shows the pooled symbols of LXXXVII and LXXVIII regrouped into CLXV.

title: A Roman product is not a landmark
description: Shows that V × L is 250, which needs several symbols, CCL, instead of a single landmark.

title: Build 302 tile by tile
description: Shows the core move of the Roman numeral builder: placing landmark tiles until the running total matches the target 302.

topic_name: The Egyptian System: Landmarks that are Powers of Ten
title: Ten of each makes the next
description: Shows the Egyptian landmarks 1, 10, 100, 1000, each one 10 times the one before.

topic_name: The Egyptian System: Landmarks that are Powers of Ten
title: Read an Egyptian numeral by adding
description: Shows 3 lotuses, no coils, 4 heels and 6 strokes read as 3000 + 40 + 6 = 3046.

topic_name: The Egyptian System: Landmarks that are Powers of Ten
title: Read an Egyptian numeral
description: Shows reading an Egyptian numeral by adding the value of every symbol: 2 coils, 7 heels, 6 strokes is 276.

title: 89 in base 5
description: Shows 89 written in the base 5 system as 3 hexagons, 2 squares and 4 triangles.

title: Base 3 landmarks
description: Shows that the landmarks of a base 3 system are 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, each 3 times the one before.

title: Five counters fuse into one
description: Shows the core move of the base grouping builder in base 5: five counters in the 1 bin fuse into one counter in the 5 bin.

topic_name: Adding and Multiplying with a Base
title: Ten strokes make one heel
description: Shows regrouping in Egyptian addition: 15 strokes become 1 heel and 5 strokes.

topic_name: Adding and Multiplying with a Base
title: A coil times a heel is a lotus
description: Shows that multiplying two Egyptian landmarks, 100 × 10, gives another landmark, 1000.

topic_name: Adding and Multiplying with a Base
title: Times 10 moves every symbol up
description: Shows that multiplying 121 by 10 turns every symbol into the next landmark, giving 1210.

topic_name: Adding and Multiplying with a Base
title: Ten ones carry to the tens line
description: Shows the carry on the counting board when adding 2907 and 43: 7 ones and 3 ones make 10 ones, which become one counter on the tens line.

topic_name: Adding and Multiplying with a Base
title: Trade 10 counters for 1
description: Shows the column board's single action: 10 counters in one column traded for 1 counter in the next column.

title: 4000 grouped into powers of 60
description: Shows 4000 grouped as one 3600, six 60s and 40 ones.

title: 60 sixties make one 3600
description: Shows regrouping in base 60: (2) × 3600 + (75) × 60 + 10 becomes (3) × 3600 + (15) × 60 + 10.

title: The place tells the landmark
description: Shows 3725 written as 1, 2, 5 in three places, where the position alone says 3600s, 60s or 1s.

title: Write 132 in base 60
description: Shows writing a number in the base 60 place system: 132 is two 60s and 12, written 2 | 12.

topic_name: The Empty Place: Mesopotamian, Mayan and Chinese Numerals
title: One numeral, two numbers
description: Shows that the marks 2 and 5 with a gap could mean 125 or 7205, because a blank place is easy to miss.

topic_name: The Empty Place: Mesopotamian, Mayan and Chinese Numerals
title: Read a Mayan numeral
description: Shows a Mayan numeral read from the bottom up: one bar, three dots, two dots give 5 + 60 + 720 = 785.

topic_name: The Empty Place: Mesopotamian, Mayan and Chinese Numerals
title: A shell holds the empty place
description: Shows 361 in Mayan numerals: one dot, a shell, one dot, stacked from top to bottom.

topic_name: The Empty Place: Mesopotamian, Mayan and Chinese Numerals
title: 5072 in rod numerals
description: Shows 5072 in Chinese rod numerals: heng rods for thousands and tens, zong rods for units, a blank for the empty hundreds.

topic_name: The Empty Place: Mesopotamian, Mayan and Chinese Numerals
title: An empty column breaks the number
description: Shows the core move of the zero placeholder breaker: leaving the 10s column empty makes 305 read as 35, while a 0 keeps it 305.

topic_name: The Hindu Number System and Zero
title: The 0 holds the hundreds place
description: Shows 4072 as one digit per place, with 0 filling the empty hundreds place.

topic_name: The Hindu Number System and Zero
title: Zero follows the rules of numbers
description: Shows that 0 is a number with its own arithmetic: 25 + 0 = 25, 25 × 0 = 0, and 25 − 25 = 0.

topic_name: The Hindu Number System and Zero
title: 19 in base 8
description: Shows 19 grouped into eights: two groups of 8 and 3 left over, written 23 in base 8.

topic_name: The Hindu Number System and Zero
title: Sort number systems by two questions
description: Shows the core move of the numeral system sorter: the same number in three systems dropped into a grid that asks about place value and a zero symbol.

title: Three ideas behind our numerals
description: Sums up the chapter in three ideas: a base, place value, and zero.
